newsitem.title: USA: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates up in wk--Freddie Mac.
newsitem.headline: US 30-, 15-yr mortgage rates up in wk--Freddie Mac.

text.p: Average commitment rates on 30-year fixed-rate home mortgages rose to 7.65 percent in the week ending February 28 from 7.56 the previous week, while 15-year mortgages increased to 7.15 percent from 7.06 percent, Freddie Mac said Thursday.
One-year adjustable-rate mortgages also inched up to 5.49 percent from 5.45 percent last week, it said.
A year ago, the 30-year loan rate averaged 7.41 percent, the 15-year 6.87 percent and the ARM 5.38 percent.

"Interest rates started rising when Alan Greenspan (chairman) of the Federal Reserve advised the Senate Banking Committee that although the economy is in generally good shape, the financial markets should use caution," Freddie Mac chief economist Robert Van Order said.
"Consequently, not only are interest rates up this week, but we expect they will rise even more by next week, perhaps to about 7.75 percent," Van Order added.
The central bank chairman on Wednesday gave the seminannual Humphrey Hawkins economic testimony to Congress.
On Friday, the National Association of Realtors will issue U.S. January existing home sales data.
Lenders charged an average 1.7 percent in fees and points on both 30- and 15-year loans, unchanged from last week. They charged 1.4 percent on the ARM, also unchanged from the prior week.
Freddie Mac is a corporation chartered by Congress that buys mortgages from lenders and packages them into securities for investors.
